The treatment

What it is

Laser hair reduction uses light that is absorbed by the pigment in the hair. The heat damages the hair follicle and slows regrowth.

It gives long-term reduction, not permanent removal. Treatment is done as a course of sessions, because only hairs in their active growth phase respond each time. Hair that grows back is usually finer and lighter.

Hormonal conditions such as PCOS can drive hair growth and affect how well treatment works. Blood tests, if needed, are done in the clinic's own laboratory.

Book a consultation

Uses

Areas commonly treated

Face

  • Upper lip
  • Chin and jawline
  • Sideburns and cheeks
  • Beard shaping

Body

  • Underarms
  • Arms and legs
  • Back and chest
  • Bikini line

Laser works best on dark hair. Very light, grey or white hair has little pigment for the laser to act on, so it responds poorly.

Safety

Before you decide

Indian skin

Darker skin contains more melanin, which also absorbs laser light. Settings that suit your skin type lower the risk of burns or patchy pigmentation, which is why the skin and hair are assessed before treatment.

Possible side effects

Temporary redness and slight swelling around the hair follicles are common. Burns, blistering and changes in skin colour are less common risks. The doctor will go through them with you.

Before your consultation

Tell the doctor about medicines you take, recent tanning or sun exposure, and any hormonal conditions.

Questions

Common questions

Didn't see yours? Ask it on WhatsApp before you book.

Ask a question
Is laser hair reduction permanent?

It gives long-term reduction rather than permanent removal. It is done as a course of sessions, and hair that grows back is usually finer and lighter. Hormonal conditions such as PCOS can affect hair growth and how well treatment works, so this is discussed at the consultation.

Is laser treatment safe on Indian skin?

It can be, with settings that suit your skin type. Darker skin contains more melanin, which also absorbs laser light, so the wrong settings raise the risk of burns or patchy pigmentation. Suitability is assessed at a consultation.

Does it work on all hair colours?

It works best on dark hair. Very light, grey or white hair has little pigment for the laser to act on, so it responds poorly.

Can men have laser hair reduction?

Yes. Beard shaping, back and chest are common areas for men.

Does the clinic have a laboratory and pharmacy?

Yes. Blood tests are done in the clinic's own laboratory, and the clinic has its own pharmacy.
